summary: Ontario tower at the Beaverhouse Entry Station of Quetico Provincial Park. A volunteer list counts it as standing; its cab has blown off. No build date found.

facts.status_note: The cab shown in a Firelookout.ca photo has since blown off.

access.note: A volunteer list asks visitors not to climb the towers, which the MNR no longer maintains.

events.note: Volunteer list says the Ontario MNR decided, as of 2013, to remove many still-standing towers. The list names this tower; the decision is not confirmed for it.

evidence.supports: Still-standing list places the Beaverhouse Tower at the Beaverhouse Entry Station
evidence.quote: 51- Beaverhouse Tower- Beaverhouse Entry Station, Ont.

evidence.supports: The Ontario MNR decided, as of 2013, to remove many still-standing towers
evidence.quote: The Ontario MNR has decided, as of 2013, to remove many of these still standing towers.

evidence.supports: The MNR no longer maintains the towers and asks visitors not to climb
evidence.quote: The MNR no longer maintains them so please refrain from climbing.

evidence.supports: Quetico Provincial Park is served by six entry stations
evidence.quote: Quetico is served by six entry stations.

evidence.supports: Beaverhouse Lake is one of three lakes that provide northern entry opportunities, accessible by road
evidence.quote: Beaverhouse Lake, French Lake and Nym Lake provide northern entry opportunities and are accessible by road.

evidence.supports: The management plan is for Quetico Provincial Park
evidence.quote: This document provides policy direction for the protection, development and management of Quetico Provincial Park and its resources.

evidence.supports: Firelookout.ca gives the address as Rainy River, Ontario

evidence.quote: The cab pictured here has since blown off.

corrections.current: The tower still stands, but its cab is gone (Firelookout.ca).
corrections.proposed: The cab shown in a Firelookout.ca photo has since blown off.
corrections.why: The Firelookout.ca page says only that the pictured cab has since blown off; it does not say the tower stands. The standing claim comes from the volunteer still-standing list.

notes_for_editor: Volunteer list is undated, so 'still standing' is only as current as that list. Firelookout.ca shows Year Built and Tower Type as N/A. No staffing or fire history found. Brief status_note overstates the Firelookout.ca page (see corrections). A Friends of Quetico Facebook post, seen only in a search snippet, mentions a fire tower removed around 1979-80 on a lake whose name starts 'Sturg'; the post would not open, and it may not concern this tower. Check. Firelookout.ca's 'Rainy River' is a broad place name; the volunteer list gives the entry station.
